issues.subject: Compile Weekly: Tallow 4 drops its config file
issues.text:
COMPILE WEEKLY
Front-end and web platform news. Thursday {date}

View in your browser: https://compileweekly.example/issues/compile-weekly-tallow-4-drops-its-config-file

Hi all. A busy week: a major bundler release, a long-awaited CSS feature finally shipping without a flag, and the results of the State of Interfaces survey, which closed on Monday 19 October with 14,200 responses.

TOP STORIES

Tallow 4.0 is out, and the config file is optional
The Tallow team shipped version 4 on Tuesday. Most projects can now delete their config entirely: entry points are read from package.json and the dev server picks a port on its own. Build times on their benchmark app dropped from 9.1s to 3.4s. The migration guide lists six breaking changes, mostly around plugin hooks.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/tallow-4-0-is-out-and-the-config-file-is-optional

State of Interfaces 2026: first results
Early numbers from this year's survey: 61% of respondents now use container queries in production, up from 34%, and component libraries built on unstyled primitives are the most common choice for new projects. Full results are due on 5 November.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/state-of-interfaces-2026-first-results

Anchor positioning, a practical guide
Leila Brandt rebuilds a tooltip, a dropdown and a context menu with anchor positioning and no JavaScript for placement. She is honest about where it still falls short: flipping near the viewport edge needs care.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/anchor-positioning-a-practical-guide

IN BRIEF

Fernlight 2.3 adds sharding for browser tests
Split a suite across machines with one flag. The team reports a 40-minute suite running in 11 on four runners.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/fernlight-2-3-adds-sharding-for-browser-tests

Cedar UI 5 beta
The component library moves its styles to cascade layers, so your own CSS wins without !important.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/cedar-ui-5-beta

Jobs: Senior Front-end Engineer, Larkspur Health (London, hybrid)
React, TypeScript, accessibility a must. £85k to £95k.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/jobs/larkspur-health-senior-frontend

Thanks for reading, see you next Thursday.

Owen Pratt, editor

--

issues.subject: Compile Weekly: a closer look at view transitions
issues.text:
COMPILE WEEKLY
Front-end and web platform news. Thursday {date}

View in your browser: https://compileweekly.example/issues/compile-weekly-a-closer-look-at-view-transitions

Hi all. This week's issue leans towards motion, partly because three of the best pieces I read were about it. As ever, reply to this email if you've written something you'd like us to see.

TOP STORIES

View transitions across pages, one year on
Jun Matsuda surveys 30 sites that adopted cross-document view transitions and finds the most common mistake is animating too much: whole pages sliding in when only the header needed to move. His rule of thumb is one shared element per transition.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/view-transitions-across-pages-one-year-on

Quire 3 rewrites its editor
The headless CMS has replaced its rich-text editor with one built on the browser's own editing APIs. Paste from word processors is noticeably cleaner, and the bundle shrank by 140 KB.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/quire-3-rewrites-its-editor

Reduced motion is not no motion
A short, sensible post on honouring reduced-motion preferences by swapping slides for fades rather than removing feedback altogether.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/reduced-motion-is-not-no-motion

IN BRIEF

Pebble 1.0, a tiny date library
Under 3 KB, immutable, formats with the platform's own Intl APIs. No time zone database of its own.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/pebble-1-0-a-tiny-date-library

The cost of a font, measured
A team removed two weights of their brand font and gained 180 ms on their slowest pages.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/the-cost-of-a-font-measured

Jobs: Front-end Developer, Northgate Libraries (Manchester)
Public sector, accessible by default, four-day week trial. £52k to £58k.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/jobs/northgate-libraries-frontend

Until next week.

Owen Pratt, editor

issues.subject: Compile Weekly: forms without the form library
issues.text:
COMPILE WEEKLY
Front-end and web platform news. Thursday {date}

View in your browser: https://compileweekly.example/issues/compile-weekly-forms-without-the-form-library

Hi all. Forms are the theme this week, and there is a quietly important accessibility fix in the second story. The jobs section is a little longer than usual.

TOP STORIES

Forms without the form library
Ravi Chandran deletes a 30 KB form library from a checkout flow and replaces it with native constraint validation and a few dozen lines of glue. The post covers custom error messages, async checks and keeping focus where the user expects it.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/forms-without-the-form-library

Screen readers and live regions, retested
A team retested live region announcements across five screen reader and browser pairs. Polite regions inserted after page load are still announced inconsistently; their advice is to render the region empty on load and change its text later.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/screen-readers-and-live-regions-retested

Lighthouse scores are not a goal
An opinion piece, but a good one, on why teams chasing a perfect score shipped slower pages for real users.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/lighthouse-scores-are-not-a-goal

IN BRIEF

Tallow 3.9 fixes a source map regression
If your stack traces pointed at the wrong line last week, upgrade.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/tallow-3-9-fixes-a-source-map-regression

A tidy guide to the popover attribute
What it gives you for free (light dismiss, top layer, focus return) and what it doesn't.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/a-tidy-guide-to-the-popover-attribute

Jobs: two roles at Brightwater Energy (Remote, UK)
Mid and senior front-end engineers for their customer app. £60k to £90k.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/jobs/brightwater-energy

Thanks for reading.

Owen Pratt, editor

issues.subject: Compile Weekly: the state of CSS nesting
issues.text:
COMPILE WEEKLY
Front-end and web platform news. Thursday {date}

View in your browser: https://compileweekly.example/issues/compile-weekly-the-state-of-css-nesting

Hi all. A shorter issue than usual this week, but every link earned its place. Our thanks to the readers who sent in corrections on last week's piece about popovers.

TOP STORIES

Native CSS nesting, two years in
Martha Quayle looks at how teams actually use native nesting now that preprocessors are optional. Most keep it to one level; the ones who went deeper regret it. The section on specificity surprises is worth bookmarking.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/native-css-nesting-two-years-in

Fernlight 2.0 released
The test runner now drives real browsers by default and ships a trace viewer that shows the DOM at every step. Upgrading from 1.x took the author of the release notes an afternoon on a large app.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/fernlight-2-0-released

Why your hydration is slow
A walk through a profile of a server-rendered app where 70% of hydration time went to a date-formatting helper called 4,000 times.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/why-your-hydration-is-slow

IN BRIEF

Cedar UI 4.6
Adds a combobox that works properly with screen readers. Finally.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/cedar-ui-4-6

Image formats in 2026, a summary table
Which format to serve for photos, screenshots and icons, and the browser support for each.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/image-formats-in-2026-a-summary-table

Jobs: Design Engineer, Holm & Rye (London)
Small studio, mostly cultural clients. £65k to £75k.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/jobs/holm-and-rye-design-engineer

Back next Thursday.

Owen Pratt, editor

issues.subject: Compile Weekly: shipping less JavaScript
issues.text:
COMPILE WEEKLY
Front-end and web platform news. Thursday {date}

View in your browser: https://compileweekly.example/issues/compile-weekly-shipping-less-javascript

Hi all. If there is a theme this week it is deleting code. Two of the top stories are about removing things, and the third is about measuring what is left.

TOP STORIES

We removed our client-side router
An e-commerce team went back to full page loads with view transitions and saw interaction latency fall on low-end phones. The write-up is careful about what they lost: some state between pages now lives in the URL.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/we-removed-our-client-side-router

Measuring interaction latency in the field
A practical guide to collecting interaction timings from real users, sampling them sensibly and spotting the handful of slow handlers that cause most of the pain.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/measuring-interaction-latency-in-the-field

Tallow plugin API, explained
If you maintain a Tallow plugin, this explainer from the core team covers the hooks and the order they run in.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/tallow-plugin-api-explained

IN BRIEF

Pebble 1.2
Adds relative time formatting ('3 days ago') using the platform's own APIs.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/pebble-1-2

A checklist for dark mode
Twenty items, from images with transparent backgrounds to focus rings that vanish on dark surfaces.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/a-checklist-for-dark-mode

Jobs: Senior Engineer, Web Platform, Fieldfare (Edinburgh or remote)
Build tooling and performance. £90k to £105k.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/jobs/fieldfare-web-platform

Until next week.

Owen Pratt, editor

issues.subject: Compile Weekly: container queries in the real world
issues.text:
COMPILE WEEKLY
Front-end and web platform news. Thursday {date}

View in your browser: https://compileweekly.example/issues/compile-weekly-container-queries-in-the-real-world

Hi all. This week's lead story is the most thorough piece on container queries I've seen. There's also a good, slightly grumpy post about dependency updates.

TOP STORIES

Container queries in the real world
Nina Halvorsen audits a design system of 120 components and moves 38 of them from viewport media queries to container queries. The before-and-after screenshots of a sidebar card are the clearest explanation of why this matters.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/container-queries-in-the-real-world

Your dependencies are a schedule
A maintainer argues that teams should update dependencies on a fixed weekly rhythm rather than in quarterly panics, and shares the small script they use to do it.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/your-dependencies-are-a-schedule

Subgrid for form layouts
Labels and inputs that line up across separate fieldsets, with no fixed widths. Short and practical.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/subgrid-for-form-layouts

IN BRIEF

Quire 2.8
Scheduled publishing now respects the editor's time zone instead of the server's.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/quire-2-8

Free workshop: testing for keyboard users
Ninety minutes online, run by a screen reader user. Recordings available afterwards.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/link/free-workshop-testing-for-keyboard-users

Jobs: Front-end Engineer, Wren Pensions (Leeds)
Accessibility-first team, hybrid. £55k to £65k.

Read more: https://compileweekly.example/jobs/wren-pensions-frontend

Thanks for reading.

Owen Pratt, editor
